# Community Archive

> Community Archive is a public, searchable collection of Twitter/X archives. Use this file as the canonical starting point for agents, researchers, and developers.

Canonical site: https://www.community-archive.org
Source repository: https://github.com/TheExGenesis/community-archive

## Start here

- [Docs and access guide](https://www.community-archive.org/docs): Human-readable overview of the bulk dump, API, and raw archives.
- [API v1 OpenAPI specification](https://analytics.community-archive.org/v1/openapi.json): Machine-readable schema for the current keyed API.
- [API v1 migration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheExGenesis/community-archive/main/docs/api-v1-migration.md): Call-by-call mapping from the legacy Supabase REST API to v1, with paging examples.
- [API keys](https://www.community-archive.org/settings/api-keys): Sign in and create a personal key for v1.
- [Semantic search API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheExGenesis/community-archive/main/docs/api-doc.md#semantic-search-api): Open, keyless vector search over the corpus at https://embed.tweetstack.app.
- [Agent and schema guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheExGenesis/community-archive/main/docs/agents.md): Tables, relationships, fields, and common query patterns.
- [Legacy API guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheExGenesis/community-archive/main/docs/api-doc.md): REST and JavaScript examples for the Supabase API, which is retired on 2026-11-19.
- [Legacy interactive API reference](https://www.community-archive.org/api/reference) and [legacy OpenAPI specification](https://www.community-archive.org/openapi.json): the PostgREST API.
- [Examples](https://github.com/TheExGenesis/community-archive/tree/main/docs/examples): Python examples and a canonical notebook.

## Choose the right data access method

1. Filtered or application queries: use the Community Archive API v1 with a personal key. The public Supabase REST API still works until 2026-11-19, when it is retired; do not start new work on it.
2. Bulk analysis: download the daily consent-safe Parquet package from the [latest release](https://github.com/TheExGenesis/community-archive/releases/latest).
3. Search by meaning: `POST https://embed.tweetstack.app/embeddings/search` (no key), then hydrate the returned tweet IDs through API v1.
4. One user's original processed archive: authenticated owners may use the policy-aware web endpoint for their own archive.

## Bulk dump

The daily package contains enriched `tweets.parquet`, separate `profiles.parquet`,
and `manifest.json` with row counts, schemas, and checksums. It includes eligible
members and checks current PostgreSQL membership and opt-outs before publication,
including consent for referenced authors.

Start from the [latest GitHub release](https://github.com/TheExGenesis/community-archive/releases/latest).
Scripts can read the stable [latest.json pointer](https://fabxmporizzqflnftavs.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/community-archive-public-export/latest.json)
and follow its `manifest_url` to the current package. GitHub lists download links;
the Parquet files remain in consent-managed storage. Superseded packages are
removed, so do not bookmark versioned file URLs. Downloads may be temporarily
withdrawn when consent changes.

## API v1 (current)

Base URL: https://analytics.community-archive.org/v1
OpenAPI 3.1: https://analytics.community-archive.org/v1/openapi.json
Key: a signed-in user creates one at https://www.community-archive.org/settings/api-keys and sends it as `Authorization: Bearer cak_...` on every request. Keys are personal; keep them server-side, never in browser code. There is no anonymous access.

Routes:

- `GET /v1/tweets/{tweet_id}`: one tweet. `GET /v1/tweets?ids=A,B,C`: up to 100 tweets in request order.
- `GET /v1/tweets?since=&until=`: every tweet created in a window of at most 31 days, keyset-paged.
- `GET /v1/tweets/search?q=&from_user=&reply_to_user=&since=&until=&limit=&offset=`: full-text search (offset up to 5,000, returns `next_offset`).
- `GET /v1/accounts/{account}` and `GET /v1/accounts?ids=|usernames=`: profile and membership flags. `{account}` is a numeric account ID or a username; a numeric username needs an `@` prefix.
- `GET /v1/accounts/{account}/tweets?order=asc|desc&since=&until=&exclude_replies=&exclude_retweets=`: account timeline.
- `GET /v1/accounts/{account}/likes`, `/followers`, `/following`: archive-derived likes and follow edges.
- `GET /v1/members`: every current member.
- `GET /v1/me`: the calling key and its limits.

Rules:

- Responses are `{"data": ..., "next_cursor": ..., "request_id": ...}`; errors are `{"error": {"code", "message"}, "request_id"}`.
- Page by passing `next_cursor` back as `cursor` until it is `null`. Do not stop on a short or empty page. Up to 200 tweets, 500 likes or follows, or 1,000 members per page.
- Each tweet carries `tweet_id`, `account_id`, `username`, `account_display_name`, `avatar_media_url`, `created_at` (ISO 8601 UTC), `full_text`, `favorite_count`, `retweet_count`, `reply_to_tweet_id`, `reply_to_user_id`, `reply_to_username`, `quoted_tweet_id`, `retweeted_tweet_id`, `conversation_id`, `media[]`, `urls[]`, `mentioned_account_ids[]`. IDs are strings.
- Deleted and opted-out tweets are omitted.
- Limits: 60 requests a minute and 20,000 a day per key, and two requests in flight per account. On `429` or `503`, wait `Retry-After` seconds and retry. A `422` means the query exceeded its budget; narrow it, for example with a date range.

cURL example:

```bash
export CA_API_KEY='cak_...'

curl --get "https://analytics.community-archive.org/v1/accounts/exgenesis/tweets" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CA_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "order=desc" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=5"
```

## Semantic search API (open, no key)

Base URL: https://embed.tweetstack.app
Search: `POST /embeddings/search` with a JSON body. No API key; 100 requests a minute per client, with `X-RateLimit-*` headers and `429` beyond that.
Coverage: the consent-filtered serving corpus (about 18.5 million tweets), refreshed every ten minutes. `GET /embeddings/stats` reports `vectorCount` and `dimension`.
Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-4B`, 1,024 dimensions. Send `searchTerm` (text) or a `vector` from the same model, not both.

Body fields: `searchTerm` or `vector`; `k` (default 10, up to 1,000); `threshold` (minimum cosine similarity, default 0.65); `filter`; `with_payload` (default true); `with_vector` (default false).

Filter: `{"must": [...], "should": [...], "must_not": [...]}` (AND, OR, NOT). Conditions are `{"key": "username", "match": {"value": "exgenesis"}}` (exact), `{"key": "text", "match": {"text": "archive"}}` (case-insensitive substring), or `{"key": "created_at", "range": {"gte": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z", "lt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}}` (`gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`; ISO 8601 or Unix milliseconds). Filter on `account_id`, `username`, `account_display_name`, or `created_at` for speed; a `text` substring filter is applied after retrieval and can return fewer than `k`.

Response: `{"success": true, "results": [{"key": "<tweet_id>", "distance": <cosine similarity, higher is closer>, "metadata": {"account_id", "username", "account_display_name", "created_at", "text", "original_text", "reply_to_tweet_id", ...}}], "count": N}`, best match first. Errors are `{"success": false, "error": "..."}` with HTTP 400 for an invalid body. `key` is the tweet ID; fetch full tweets with `GET /v1/tweets?ids=A,B,C`. `POST /embeddings/retrieve` with `{"ids": [...], "with_vector": true}` returns stored metadata and embeddings for up to 1,000 tweet IDs.

cURL example:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://embed.tweetstack.app/embeddings/search \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"searchTerm": "you can just do things", "k": 10, "threshold": 0.6,
       "filter": {"must": [{"key": "username", "match": {"value": "exgenesis"}}]}}'
```

## Legacy Supabase REST API (retired on 2026-11-19)

The PostgREST API below is retired on 2026-11-19 in favour of API v1. It keeps working until then. Existing integrations should move before that date using the migration guide linked above.

API base URL: https://fabxmporizzqflnftavs.supabase.co
REST base URL: https://fabxmporizzqflnftavs.supabase.co/rest/v1
Public anon key: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJzdXBhYmFzZSIsInJlZiI6ImZhYnhtcG9yaXp6cWZsbmZ0YXZzIiwicm9sZSI6ImFub24iLCJpYXQiOjE3MjIyNDQ5MTIsImV4cCI6MjAzNzgyMDkxMn0.UIEJiUNkLsW28tBHmG-RQDW-I5JNlJLt62CSk9D_qG8

The anon key is intentionally public. Send it as both `apikey` and `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Never expose or request a service-role key.

cURL example:

```bash
export CA_API_URL='https://fabxmporizzqflnftavs.supabase.co'
export CA_ANON_KEY='eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJzdXBhYmFzZSIsInJlZiI6ImZhYnhtcG9yaXp6cWZsbmZ0YXZzIiwicm9sZSI6ImFub24iLCJpYXQiOjE3MjIyNDQ5MTIsImV4cCI6MjAzNzgyMDkxMn0.UIEJiUNkLsW28tBHmG-RQDW-I5JNlJLt62CSk9D_qG8'

curl --get "$CA_API_URL/rest/v1/enriched_tweets" \
  -H "apikey: $CA_ANON_KEY" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CA_ANON_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "select=tweet_id,username,created_at,full_text" \
  --data-urlencode "username=ilike.defenderofbasic" \
  --data-urlencode "order=created_at.desc" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=5"
```

Useful public resources:

- `enriched_tweets`: tweets joined with username, display name, conversation, quote, and avatar fields.
- `tweets`: core tweet records.
- `all_account`: account IDs, usernames, display names, and counts.
- `all_profile`: bios, websites, locations, and profile media.
- `user_directory`: directory-ready account and profile data.
- `followers`, `following`, `likes`, `liked_tweets`, `tweet_media`, `tweet_urls`, `user_mentions`, `mentioned_users`, `retweets`, `quote_tweets`, `conversations`: relationship and supporting tables.

Important API rules:

- API username casing is preserved. Use a case-insensitive `ilike` filter when the original casing is unknown. Raw archive storage paths use lowercase usernames.
- Treat Twitter IDs as strings; JavaScript numbers cannot safely represent every Twitter ID.
- Use PostgREST filters such as `username=eq.name`, `created_at=gte.2025-01-01`, and `order=created_at.desc`.
- Select only needed columns.
- Responses are capped at 1,000 rows. Paginate with `limit` and `offset` or HTTP Range headers, using a stable order.
- Bulk exports include eligible members, not every account observed in the archive.

## Individual raw archives

Raw archives are private and policy-checked at download time. Use the web
endpoint `/api/archive/<username>` while authenticated as that archive owner;
blocked owners receive no download URL.

Raw archive structure: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheExGenesis/community-archive/main/docs/archive_data.md
